hook.text: Ranked Choice Voting: one decision can look obvious until uncertainty changes the frame.

buildup.text: Ranked choice prevents the spoiler effect. A third-party candidate cannot split the vote and hand victory to the least.

discovery.text: It encourages broader appeal. Candidates need second-choice votes, so they campaign less negatively.

twist.text: Ranked Choice Voting shows that the best decision is often not the most intuitive one.

climax.text: No voting system is perfect. Ranked choice fixes spoilers but introduces new complexities. Trade-offs are inevitable.

punchline.text: Rank all, eliminate the lowest. Better than simple voting, still imperfect.

quiz.question: What problem does ranked choice voting solve?
options: The spoiler effect where similar candidates split votes and an unpopular one wins
